speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your mucous membranes, and a rash of small red spots called petechiae; can you tell me how old you are and if these symptoms have been present since birth or did they start recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia B (Christmas disease) or Hemophilia A (Factor VIII deficiency) is unlikely given the mucocutaneous bleeding pattern (epistaxis, gum bleeding, petechiae), which suggests a platelet disorder or von Willebrand disease; however, severe Vitamin K deficiency or Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC) remain possibilities. Given the age (4 years) and chronic presentation, I suspect an inherited platelet dysfunction like Glanzmann's thrombasthenia or Bernard-Soulier syndrome, or possibly von Willebrand disease. I will request a Complete Blood Count (CBC) with platelet count and smear, and a PTT/PT/INR panel to differentiate between coagulation factor deficiencies and platelet disorders. REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_diff_and_platelet_smear, PT, PTT.
